History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
45-year-old female housekeeper with 3–4 month history of painful, itchy, cracked palmar skin, now worsening and impairing work; assessment consistent with irritant/contact dermatitis.

History:
• Chief complaint: Painful, cracked skin and soreness in fingers/palms.  
• Onset & course: Began ≈3–4 months ago after starting new housekeeping job; progressively worse, particularly over last week, causing work absence x3 days.  
• Character: Dryness, fissuring, intermittent itch; occasional bleeding only after scratching.  
• Distribution: Primarily palms; mild generalized dryness on legs (long-standing, non-severe).  
• Exacerbating factors: Handling cleaning products without gloves.  
• Relieving measures tried: OTC E45 emollient and oral antihistamine—no improvement.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, constitutional symptoms, GI or GU complaints. Appetite and general well-being preserved.  
• ROS highlights: No respiratory, cardiovascular, or neurologic complaints voiced; pertinent negatives as above.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – on metformin; no complications reported.  
• Denies prior eczema, dermatitis, or other chronic skin disorders.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• E45 emollient (OTC) – topical, trial without benefit.  
• Antihistamine – name/dose/route/frequency not documented, trial without benefit.

Allergies:
• No known drug or environmental allergies reported.

Social History:
• Occupation: Hotel housekeeper; frequent exposure to cleaning chemicals; inconsistently wears protective gloves.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: “Couple of pints” beer per week (light intake).  
• Recent work impact: Off work past 3 days due to hand pain.

Family History:
• Diabetes mellitus present in family.  
• No known familial skin disorders, asthma, or bowel diseases.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed/not documented in transcript.)

Investigations:
• None ordered or reported during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected irritant/contact dermatitis of hands  
  • Plan:
    – Advise strict avoidance of irritants; mandate glove use during all cleaning tasks.  
    – Prescribe topical corticosteroid cream (potency and regimen not specified in transcript).  
    – Prescribe high-emollient moisturizer; instruct liberal application 3–4 times daily x2 weeks.  
    – Educate on skin care, hydration, and trigger avoidance.  
    – Follow-up: Re-evaluate in 10–14 days; return sooner if worsening, spreading, or no improvement.

General Plan Items:  
  • Prescription to be sent electronically to patient’s pharmacy today.  
  • Reinforce optimal diabetes control, though not directly addressed this visit.

Quality checks:

Missing/expected elements:  
• Physical examination findings and vitals not documented.  
• Full medication list with doses/frequencies not obtained.  
• Formal allergy verification (food/latex) could be expanded.  
• No objective assessment of diabetic control (e.g., A1c) discussed.

Internal conflicts: None noted.

Transcript quality: Clear dialogue; minor background/overlap but clinically adequate.
